start.quote: There is a small carpark, for about 4 vehicles, and an information panel here.

end.name: small carpark at the saddle on Makahu Road (starting point)
end.quote: Return to your starting point by following Makahu Road

via.name: Makino-Te Puia track junction
via.quote: the track junction to Te Puia Lodge

via.name: true right of the Mohaka River
via.quote: the true right of the Mokaha River

via.name: Mangatutu Hot Springs Campsite
via.quote: Mangatutu Hot Springs Campsite is at the end of the track.

evidence: A short distance after Makahu Road enters the park it climbs to a saddle. It is from this point the track to Makino Hut leaves the road.
If you went to Makino Hut, return back down Makino Track until you reach the track junction to Te Puia Lodge.
From Te Puia Lodge, follow the track down the true right of the Mokaha River to the end of Makahu Road.
Return to your starting point by following Makahu Road (either walking or arranging transport).
The whole loop can also be done in reverse: Mangatutu to Te Puia, to Makino then out to the road.

doubts: The start is the small carpark at the saddle where the Makino Hut track leaves Makahu Road. F1 ('where an unnamed track meets Makahu Road') is taken to be that point because the Makino Track is not a named map track while Te Puia Track is, but F1 lies about 1 km from Mangatutu Hot Springs Campsite and could instead be near the road end ('The Gums'); the text gives no distance between the saddle and the road end. Makino Hut is a short out-and-back spur (15-20 min) off the circuit from the Makino-Te Puia junction. The last leg back along Makahu Road may be walked or done by transport. The page says the loop can be done in reverse but names no clockwise/anticlockwise direction. Te Puia Lodge has no entry in names or links. No distance given; the 6-7 hrs is DOC's summary time and may not include the road walk.
